mappings.note: Naming irrigation as the timed supply of water is one of the practices that increase crop production. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, because nothing here is about conserving the water, only about identifying the practice.
The khurpi as the hand tool for weeding is a crop-production operation. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1: manual weeding is the alternative to weedicides, so no agrochemical restraint is tested.

The sprayer is defined here by the weedicide it delivers, which puts the item on the controlled-use-of-pesticides outcome. Deliberately different from the khurpi item above, where the method is mechanical and no chemical is involved.
Picking the rabi crop out of a list is the kharif/rabi classification named verbatim in this outcome. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, because the pupil sorts crops rather than carries out a practice.
The cultivator used for ploughing is a tillage implement in the production cycle. Not C-SCI3.1-LO-1, which asks for a model to be built and explained, not a machine's use recalled.

The four statements contrast fertiliser with manure and humus, so the item sits on the fertiliser judgement outcome. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, because the pupil is testing statements for truth rather than sorting materials into classes.

Choosing the sprinkler system for uneven land is the water-saving choice, which is using a resource judiciously. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, which fits the plain naming of an irrigation method (see the rotating-nozzle item) rather than a suitability judgement.
Winnowing by wind is a post-harvest production practice. Not C-SCI2.1-LO-1, because no investigation is planned or conducted, a known method is recalled.
Broadcasting as hand-scattering of seed is a sowing method within crop production. Not C-SCI4.2-LO-1, since no design or creative planning is being asked for.
Placing a bacteriophage in the virus class is a classification of microorganisms, the outcome's own example. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, because no disease or phenomenon is being traced to a cause.
Sequencing threshing after harvesting is knowledge of the production cycle. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1: nothing is being classified, a step order is being recalled.
The combine doing harvesting and threshing together is farm machinery in the production chain. Not C-SCI3.1-LO-1, which requires constructing a working model.
Gunny bags as a grain-storage method is applied crop management after harvest. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, because no resource restraint or hazard is at issue, only a container.

Legumes enriching soil with nitrogen relates an observed effect to its cause, the pattern of C-SCI2.2-LO-1. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, which would fit a decision about fertiliser use rather than the mechanism behind the enrichment.
Raising soil fertility by manure, fertiliser or rotation is exactly the controlled-input judgement in C-SCI4.1-LO-1. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, because the item asks what to do, not why it works.
Silos as bulk grain storage is applied post-harvest management, grouping with the gunny-bag item. Not C-SCI3.1-LO-1, because no model is constructed.

Neem leaves protecting stored grain is a household application of science, grouped with the other storage items. C-SCI4.1-LO-1 was rejected narrowly: the item names a traditional method, it does not ask the pupil to restrain chemical use.

Naming Plasmodium as the malarial parasite ties a disease to its causative agent. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, which is reserved here for items sorting microorganisms into useful and harmful or into their groups.
Picking the useful microorganism from a list of four is the useful/harmful classification named verbatim in this outcome. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, because no single disease is being explained.
Fermentation as the conversion of sugar to alcohol is a process to be explained. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, because the item is about the chemical change, not about which organism is useful.
Loosening and turning the soil, i.e. ploughing, is the first production practice. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, since tillage is not one of the inputs the environmental outcome restrains.

Rhizobium in root nodules is the textbook useful microorganism, so the useful/harmful classification fits. Kept apart from the legume-enrichment item above, which asks for the causal effect rather than the organism's standing.

Identifying sprinkler irrigation from its rotating nozzles is method recall inside crop production. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, which was used for the uneven-land item where the water-saving judgement is the point.
Separating weeds from non-weeds sorts plants by their characteristics, a classification of organisms. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, which covers the removal practice rather than recognising the plant.
Knowing that paddy is transplanted matches a crop to a sowing practice, an application that raises yield. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, because the crop is not being placed in a seasonal class.
Hepatitis B traced to its causative organism is a disease-to-cause link. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, since the pupil is not classifying organisms as useful or harmful.
Recognising viruses as the group on the living/non-living borderline is a classification by characteristics. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-2, because no process is being explained, a group is being placed.

A legume needing no nitrogenous fertiliser is precisely the controlled-use-of-fertilisers judgement. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, which fits the mechanism items; here the pupil must act on it by withholding an input.

Naming the bacterium that turns alcohol into acetic acid identifies a useful microorganism. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-2, which was used for the fermentation item where the chemical change itself is the question.
Picking the bacterial disease links an illness to the kind of agent that causes it. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, because the options are diseases, not organisms to be sorted.

Reading leaf-spot symptoms back to a disease and its causative agent is cause-finding from evidence, the core of C-SCI2.2-LO-1. Not C-SCI2.1-LO-1, because the observation is given, no investigation is conducted.
Explaining why beans thrive in nitrogen-poor soil through Rhizobium nodules is causal reasoning about a phenomenon. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1: the item asks for the reason, not for a fertiliser decision.

Yeast used in bread or alcohol production is the useful-microorganism side of the classification. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, because the item names the product, it does not ask the pupil to apply the process at home.

Who discovered Bacillus anthracis is a story of scientific discovery, the only outcome in the frame about the history of science. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, because no organism is being classified, a discoverer is being named.
Excluding the non-protozoan from a list sorts microorganisms into their groups. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, because no disease is being traced.
A repeat of the ploughing definition; loosening the soil is a crop-production practice. Same code as its duplicate earlier in the chapter for the same reason.
